PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-guardian-leader-armor
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
CORRODED BLACK-IRON ARMOR AND HORNED HELMET — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe ingredients sheet isolating the complete battle panoply of Hell's Guardian Leader—Hell's Champion—as worn at THE GATE before Jesus arrives: full corroded black-iron plate harness plus horned-crest helmet, presented as production costume reference for a photoreal live-action biblical epic. Frame as multi-panel wardrobe construction study on a towering matching eight-foot masculine silhouette (or seamless dark armor stand with correct proportions), not a celebrity likeness and not a separate character sheet. Panels: (1) frontal three-quarter torso-and-head so the helmet, gorget, breastplate, pauldrons, and gauntlets read clearly; (2) full-body standing pose armor complete from greaves to crest; (3) strict side profile locking helmet silhouette, horn projection, cuisse depth, and sabaton profile; (4) rear-head and rear-costume view locking spine plates, cape or mail drape if any, and the back of the horned helm—never place a face on the rear of the head. One face exists only on the front of the head if the wearer's face is partially visible beneath the helm opening.

Material language: extreme-age black iron gone nearly obsidian, surfaces eaten by millennia of corrosion into flaking oxide crusts of charcoal, dull graphite, and sickly dark brown. Patches of deep pitting and freckled rust blooms along plate edges, rivet lines, and underarm articulation. Ancient battle damage mapped consistently across every panel: long diagonal score gouges across the left pauldron and breastplate as if struck by a heavy edge; nested dent clusters over the solar plexus and right cuisse; hairline stress cracks at the elbow cops and knee cops; missing or bent rivets leaving empty sockets; dried blood crusted into seams, under the gorget rim, and in the engraved recesses of the breast—old brown-black blood, not fresh red, as if from eons of slaughter. Metal is thick and heavy, not ornamental fantasy chrome; plates stack with functional overlap, leather straps blackened and cracked, iron buckles fused half-shut by corrosion, and short lengths of coarse mail (blackened rings, some broken) at the armpits, inner elbows, and skirt hem for flex.

Helmet construction (hero piece of the set): full closed bascinet-like war helm in the same corroded black iron, face aperture deep and shadowed so hollow eye sockets can later read as burning red fire when the character is lit—here the sockets remain dark cavities with residual soot and heat-stain, ready for red-fire continuity. A horned crest rises from the crown: two curved lateral horns of dark iron or fused bone-iron hybrid, tips chipped and asymmetrical from age, base plates riveted through a raised crest ridge that runs front-to-back. Helm shows impact scars on the brow and right temporal plate; chin and cheek defenses are scarred; interior leather lining visible only as a thin dark rim at the neck. No second face on the back of the helm—only smooth (if pitted) rear bowl and crest spine. Optional thin dark hair or matted strands may peek at the nape under the rear view for silhouette lock, never a second visage.

Body harness detail: massive breastplate molded for a brute eight-foot frame, slightly flared at the waist to an articulated fauld of overlapping lames; pauldrons oversized and brutal, left shoulder more scarred than right (continuity of favored guard); rerebraces and vambraces layered with leather understraps; gauntlets with knuckle ridges worn nearly smooth, fingertips dark with dried residue; cuisses, poleyns, greaves, and sabatons complete the lower half so full-body panels never float incomplete. Subtle hellish craft language only—no modern military kit, no logos, no heraldic text: faint bas-relief of writhing damned faces or torment motifs pressed into the breastplate and pauldron faces, eroded almost to ghosts, matching the iron-and-bone cruelty of Hell's Gate without readable inscriptions. Optional short ragged cloak or iron-scaled cape remnant of ash-gray and black hanging from the right pauldron for silhouette interest, edges burned and frayed.

Scale and presence: armor sized for an approximately 8'0" (244 cm) towering champion—plates oversized relative to human reference, shoulders unnaturally broad, helm volume large enough that a human would drown in it. Pose for the full-body panel is upright sentinel stance as at the Gate before confrontation: feet planted, weight centered, arms at sides or one hand resting near the hip where a massive two-handed sword or spear would hang (weapon may be omitted or shown only as a sheathed suggestion; primary focus remains wardrobe isolation). This is the intact pre-shatter state—armor whole and terrifying—not the later cracked eggshell dissolution after the Gate explodes.

Environment and lighting for the sheet: neutral-to-hellish production bay feel with physically coherent key light—cold blue torch key at approximately 2000K from upper left casting elongated metallic speculars across flaked iron, deep crimson underglow fill at approximately 3500K rising from below to catch the underside of pauldrons and fauld (Hell fortress palette: deep crimson #8B0000, obsidian #0A0A0A, cold blue #4169E1 accents). Soft volumetric smoke haze and fine ash motes in air; no pure white studio flatness. Subtle rim light of cooler blue separating the black armor from a darker charcoal background so plate edges read without washing corrosion detail. Camera language: multi-panel ingredients layout, each panel sharp enough for construction reference, mild shallow depth only on far edges, anamorphic epic still sensibility 2.39:1 overall feel but panels readable as costume bible pages. Color grade: crushed blacks, desaturated mid-grays of dead metal, blue specular highlights, dried-blood browns in seams, no cheerful gold, no modern color gels.

Texture and atmosphere: subsurface none on iron—hard speculars broken by matte oxide; leather straps show dry crackle and salt-like mineral dust; mail rings catch tiny blue highlights; dried blood has matte chalky crust in recesses. Atmosphere is toxic-cold hell air, not outdoor desert. Continuity locks repeated: corroded black iron throughout; horned crest helmet with decay; battle scars and dried blood maps identical front/side/rear; hollow eye sockets dark with heat-soot readiness for red fire; massive champion scale; intact armor state at Gate; one face only on front of head; rank-and-file guardians share the same material language but this set is more massive, more scarred, and more ornate in crest and bas-relief as the Leader's unique panoply.

Sacred-tone biblical epic production reference, photoreal live-action, physically plausible metallurgy and costume construction, exact multi-view consistency. No modern objects, no firearms, no plastic, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, no captions, no readable text or graphical UI, no anime, no cartoon, no glossy video-game sheen, no second face on the rear of the head, no cartoon horns of pure fantasy candy color—only dead black iron and age.
